text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'prod-gpu-pool-3' capacity exhaustion detected — autoscaler attempted 3 scaleups and hit quota limits. Queue length > 1200, P95 latency spike to 18s. Triggered at 03:12 UTC. Link: https://metrics.redwood/example/alert/3343219876
Alex: seeing the same in the dashboard. Prefill and kv-cache warmups spiking memory per-session. Looks like the v23 rollout increased context window defaults.
Maria: paging oncall @Alex @Jordan — are we safe to throttle new sessions?
Alex: acknowledging, oncall here. Can we get a quick diff of the rollout? Jordan, did the model change default max_ctx or enable kv-extended?
Jordan: yes — v23 default ctx_max=65k and kv_cache_shards=8 by default. We tested locally but not at global traffic.
Casey: that change would multiply KV memory per session. No surprise this blows up reserved GPU memory when many prefill-heavy requests hit.
Priya: CS reporting customer impact: increased gen failures and timeouts for 3 high-traffic tenants (Acme, BrightDesk, BetaApp). They've raised 3 support tickets.
Alex: mitigation plan A: rollback v23 to v22 for the global fleet. Plan B: immediate routing rule to send traffic to v22 for high-qps tenants. Which is faster?
Jordan: rollback hotfix is ready (revert model-ref). Requires a canary deploy then global ramp — ~8-12m. Routing rule change is instant but we need edge config push (~90s).
Maria: push routing rule first to stop new sessions from hitting v23, then start rollback canary. I'll push config now.
Maria: /deploy-edge-config set route:model=prefer:v22 --scope=global --priority=high
IncidentBot: Deploy job queued: edge-config/3321 by Maria. CI checks green.
Maria: edge change propagated in 45s. Monitoring shows new session rate to v23 dropped by 92%. Queue length trending down from 1250 -> 420.
Casey: good. But existing warm sessions on GPUs still hold large KV caches. Can we evict long-running sessions or reduce per-session cache retention?
Jordan: runtime has `kv_cache.eviction_threshold` — we can reduce to 10s TTL for inactive prefixes. Applying now.
Jordan: kubectl exec -it runtime-pod-12 -- /bin/sh -c "curl -XPOST localhost:8080/admin/config -d '{\"kv_cache.eviction_threshold\":10}'"
Alex: applied to canary runtime group. Observed memory drop on those pods ~28% in 60s. But many pods are still saturated and autoscaler still limited by provider quota.
Casey: contact cloud team to request emergency GPU quota bump or temporary reserved instances. @Priya can you file the quick-request?
Priya: filing now. Filing note: URGENT - GPU quota for project redwood-prod increase by 50 units for 2 hours. Ticket #INC-3343.
CS-Lead: I'll draft customer comms: telling affected customers we're throttling new sessions and rolling back the model; ETA 30-45m for full recovery. Any blockers?
Maria: one more thing — prefill throttling. We can reduce prefill token cap from 1024 -> 256 to reduce upstream burst pressure. Suggest pushing that immediately.
Jordan: pushed prefill cap change to route-level config. That reduced token throughput significantly; queue length fell to ~180. P95 latency now ~3.2s.
Alex: good stabilization. Autoscaler still hasn't added nodes because provider rejected due to region quota. Progress on quota?
Priya: cloud ticket acknowledged by vendor support, expedited. They provisioned 20 GPUs in 14 minutes as a temporary pool. We routed some queues to the new pool.
IncidentBot: NOTE: Emergency pool 'burst-pool-3343' created.
Casey: with the burst pool and eviction TTL drop + prefill cap, GPU memory pressure normalized. No further OOMs.
Jordan: starting rollback canary to v22 on 5% traffic now. Logs show v22 perf matching expected baseline.
Maria: ramping rollback to 50% over 10m. Keeping prefill cap and eviction TTL until fully stable.
Alex: summarizing: immediate edge routing to v22, prefill cap lowered, KV eviction TTL shortened, temporary burst GPU pool added, rollback canary started. Customer impact: timeouts reduced; CS notified tenants.
CS-Lead: customers notified at 03:28 UTC. Affected: Acme (ticket 9852), BrightDesk (9853), BetaApp (9854). We promised status updates every 20m.
Priya: handoff note for next oncall (Priya -> Jordan at 04:00 UTC): please monitor queue length < 200, ensure autoscaler has restored nodes back to target, and relax prefill cap after rollback completes and we confirm memory profiles.
Jordan: acknowledged handoff. I'll also coordinate postmortem. Initial P0->P1 classification recommended; looks like rollout config default change without canary thoroughness.
Casey: follow-ups: 1) tighten rollout gating for config changes that affect per-session memory, 2) add synthetic prefill load test to CI, 3) autoscaler should surface quota-rejected events to oncall alerts.
Alex: agreed. Creating incident ticket and assigning docs.
Alex: thanks everyone — we'll continue to monitor for 2h.
IncidentBot: Thread marked active. Next update scheduled at 03:50 UTC.
